subject: Mari
fact: Mari cleanly picked Zephyr's pocket.
source_quote: After having his pocket cleanly picked by Mari, Zephyr was looking for an opportunity to get out.

subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer drank the last of his mead and said, 'As you wish, boss!' in as disrespectful a tone as he could muster.
source_quote: He watches as Calmer drinks the last of his mead and then tells him in as disrespectful a tone Calmer can muster: 'As you wish, boss!'

subject: Sheernobb
fact: Sheernobb is a small town with the Moot Hall as its dominant building, where folks go to meet, and the road ends at the moot hall and splits into two branches, one going south and another north around the moot hall, which converge after the moot hall on the road going out of town.
source_quote: The village of Sheernobb is a small town. The dominant building is what the locals call the Moot Hall, where folks go to meet. The road ends at the moot hall and splits into two branches, one going south and another north around the moot hall. The two branches converge after the moot hall on the road going out of town.

subject: Moot Hall
fact: The Moot Hall is where folks go to meet, with two branches of the road splitting and converging around it, and most stores are located around the circle formed by the branches.
source_quote: The two branches of the moot hall form a circle around which most stores are located.

subject: Tavern
fact: The Tavern is on the south branch, just after the road coming into town ends.
source_quote: The Tavern is on the south branch, just after the road coming into town ends.

subject: Bookstore
fact: A bookstore was on the northern branch, and Grindin Books is nestled within a small cottage with a cluttered display of books and maps in its windows and a studded oak door bearing the welcoming sign, 'Welcome to the Grindin Books.'
source_quote: Zephyr remembers how a bookstore was on the northern branch. Nestled within a small cottage, Grindin Books is instantly recognizable by the cluttered display of books and maps in its windows and a studded oak door bearing the welcoming sign, 'Welcome to the Grindin Books.'

subject: Grindin Books
fact: Grindin Books is a dimly-lit bookshop constructed to the owner's specifications, with a plush chair with a clever reclining mechanism behind the counter, two glass bulbs tinted green to reduce eye strain holding burning candles, and hundreds of books crammed in every available shelf and stacked on tables and trolleys.
source_quote: This dimly-lit bookshop has been constructed to the owner's specifications, and the owner wants to read books when not helping customers. Behind the counter, a plush chair with a clever reclining mechanism lets them put their feet on an equally plush stool. Over the counter, two glass bulbs, tinted green to reduce eye strain, hold burning candles, perfectly positioned for comfortable reading. And there are books beyond counting, books crammed in every available shelf, and books stacked on tables and trolleys.

subject: Grindin Well-Read
fact: Grindin Well-Read is a gnome seated behind a desk-sized for a human, perched on a massive cushion-covered chair, who is annoyed at intrusions and says, 'My invitation to the conference was stolen! I didn’t have the opportunity to reject the invitation!'
source_quote: Behind a desk-sized for a human, perched on a massive cushion-covered chair, sits the gnome Grindin Well-Read. ... 'My invitation to the conference was stolen! I didn’t have the opportunity to reject the invitation!'

subject: Map of the Elemental Nexus
fact: A book titled 'Map of the Elemental Nexus' is visible in Grindin Books, and its knowledge about the elemental planes may prove helpful.
source_quote: Before he leaves, his eyes catch the title of a book - Map of the Elemental Nexus. A book could be purchased later. Any knowledge we can acquire about the elemental planes will prove helpful.

subject: Sequoia
fact: Sequoia leaves the bookstore and urges the group to go to the Moot Hall, saying, 'The mayor may have more information and a bigger reward.'
source_quote: The halfling leaves the bookstore and urges the group to go to the Moot Hall. 'The mayor may have more information and a bigger reward.'

subject: Statue of Keenleene
fact: A statue of Keenleene, Founder of Sheernobb, stands just before the Moot Hall entrance; it transforms into a living figure with gem-like eyes, a twitching nose, and braided gem-adorned hair that shimmers as it plays pipes and laughs heartily.
source_quote: Just before the entrance is a statue. Sequoia wants to look at it and approaches. At the statue's base, he reads a sign - 'Keenleene, Founder of Sheernobb!' ... the stone figure of Keenleene transforms, coming to life with lifelike mischief. His massive gem-like eyes sparkle brightly, and his bulky nose twitches with glee. The braided hair adorned with gemstones seems to shimmer as if alive. Keenleene begins to laugh heartily... He picks up his pipes and starts playing a lively tune...

subject: Moot Hall Interior
fact: The Moot Hall is on the largest hill in Sheernobb, with wide stone steps leading to grand stone doors carved with runes reading 'Ni te pharkalu, quo lun verra lu' (translated: 'If you see it, it’s not the right it'), opening into a chamber with three tiers of broad steps and benches, impressive woodwork, and an elder gnome asleep in an elegantly engraved oak chair with bare feet crossed over an arm.
source_quote: The Moothall is in the center of Sheernobb on the largest hill. It boasts wide stone steps leading to grand stone doors carved with runes. These doors open into the Feasting Hall... 'Ni te pharkalu, quo lun verra lu, ' with a helpful translation in common: 'If you see it, it’s not the right it.' ... The chamber's center is below Sequoia, surrounded by three tiers of broad steps, each with benches on which to sit. The woodwork within the hall is impressive... An elder gnome is seated in a large (by gnome standards) elegantly engraved oak chair with brown wrinkled skin and long white wild hair... his bare feet crossed at the ankle over one of the arms of the chair.

subject: Glennddarc
fact: Glennddarc, Headgnome of Sheernobb, is an elder gnome with brown wrinkled skin and long white wild hair, who is asleep in an oak chair, awoken by a weasel jumping into his lap, and says, 'Bandits? We have problems with giants, and you are interested in Bandits?' and suggests going to Pasmarie’s beehives.
source_quote: An elder gnome is seated in a large (by gnome standards) elegantly engraved oak chair... A weasel jumps out from seemingly nowhere into the elder gnome's lap, waking him in a grouchy yelp... 'Welcome. I am Glennddarc, Headgnome of this village...' 'Bandits? We have problems with giants, and you are interested in Bandits?' ... 'You should go to Pasmarie’s beehives if it's hunting bandits.'

subject: Pasmarie’s Beehives
fact: Pasmarie’s Beehives are located a quarter mile southeast of Sheernobb, surrounded by verdant fields and wildflowers, with hives neatly arranged in rows, paths leading to each hive, and small benches for visitors, and a small building where Pasmarie Clee, a petite gnome woman with a weathered face and apron smeared with honeycomb wax, speaks of stolen honey and 'Black Earth' raiders.
source_quote: A quarter mile southeast of Sheernobb, Zephyr and his fellow travelers arrive at Pasmarie’s Beehives. Verdant fields and wildflowers surround the farm. The hives are neatly arranged in rows... Standing in the doorway of a small building is a petite gnome woman... 'I’m Pasmarie Clee, keeper of Sheernobb’s finest beehives—or what’s left of them... a shipment of my honey... has been stolen... the attackers weren’t bandits—no, they spoke of the ‘Black Earth’ and carried weapons of stone.'

subject: Pasmarie Clee
fact: Pasmarie Clee is a petite gnome woman with a weathered face, apron smeared with honeycomb wax, who asks for help recovering stolen honey bound for Verbobonc, and offers enchanted honey as reward.
source_quote: She sets her hands on her hips. 'I’m Pasmarie Clee, keeper of Sheernobb’s finest beehives—or what’s left of them... The caravan was ambushed... the attackers weren’t bandits—no, they spoke of the ‘Black Earth’ and carried weapons of stone... I can’t offer much gold, but you’ll have my gratitude and a share of my finest enchanted honey—a taste of Sheernobb’s magic that might save your life in a pinch.'

subject: Map of the Local Area
fact: Zephyr purchases a map of the local area, which Pasmarie Clee marks to indicate the location of the last raid, a few miles to the northeast.
source_quote: Zephyr shows her the map he purchased, and she marks it. 'It had happened a few miles to the north east.'

subject: Quinna Poul
fact: Quinna Poul is a half-orc cook who points to the Gnarley Forest on Zephyr’s map as the location of the boar, saying, 'It’s a tricky little bugger.'
source_quote: Just after Zephyr finishes his breakfast, the half-orc cook, Quinna Poul points to a location on Zephyr’s map where he might find the boar. 'It’s a tricky little bugger,' she reminds him.

subject: Gnarley Forest
fact: The Gnarley Forest is a sprawling woodland straddling the borders of Verbobonc, Viscounty, Dyvers, the Domain of Greyhawk, the Wild Coast, Celene, and the Kron Hills, featuring fertile glades and valleys, and is home to ancient magic, woodsmen, Sylvan Elves, treants, and unicorns.
source_quote: The Gnarley Forest, a sprawling woodland straddling the borders of Verbobonc, Viscounty, Dyvers, the Domain of Greyhawk, the Wild Coast, Celene, and the Kron Hills, serves as a critical ecological barrier and a cultural crossroads. A part of a vast contiguous forest that includes the Welkwood, Celene, and Suss Forest, the Gnarley Forest is a natural wonder and a bastion of ancient magic and diverse communities. Its depths harbor centuries-old secrets and an array of inhabitants ranging from woodsmen and Sylvan Elves to more mystical creatures like treants and unicorns.

subject: Aunt Emma
fact: Aunt Emma is a hag who appears as an old woman wearing a brown dress, rough woolen shirt, and leather belt, luring travelers with promises of gingerbread and plum pie, and transforms into a green hag with claws, sharp teeth, and green skin when confronted.
source_quote: The old woman smiles... She’s wearing a brown dress that reaches her ankles, a rough woolen shirt dyed green, and a leather belt fastened around her waist... 'My name is Aunt Emma, and I am always looking to feed folks with my tasty treats! You will love my house! It’s made of gingerbread!' ... the illusion of her appearance disappears. She is now a green hag, her skin green, her eyes green, her hand's claws, and her mouth riddled with sharp teeth.

subject: Hat of Wizardry
fact: Zinnia finds a Hat of Wizardry in the hag’s gingerbread house, which he thinks can be sold or shared with Spugnoir.
source_quote: He finds a hat of Wizardry, which he thinks can be sold or shared with Spugnoir.

subject: The Hag's Guide to 101 Recipes Of Children
fact: A book titled 'The Hag's Guide to 101 Recipes Of Children' lies on the floor near the oven in the hag’s gingerbread house.
source_quote: He notices a book on the floor near the oven—'The Hag's Guide to 101 Recipes Of Children.'

subject: Gingerbread House
fact: The gingerbread house is a single-room dwelling with walls and roof made of gingerbread, window trim of white frosting, roof fascia decorated with sugared plums, a circular table, chairs, and a hot wood oven emitting the smell of plum pie.
source_quote: A few minutes later, they arrive at a single-room dwelling. The walls and roof are made of gingerbread. The window trim is made of white frosting. The roof fascia is decorated with white frosting and what appear to be sugared plums. From inside the house comes a pleasant smell... Inside the house is a single circular table, a few chairs, and a wood oven. The wood oven is hot, and the smell of plum pie wafts inside the room.

subject: Bronze Wood Glade
fact: The boar is found in a glade surrounded by bronze wood trees with slender trunks, reddish-brown hard bark, growing 40 feet above ground, with branches at a natural 45-degree angle bearing 8-inch leaves.
source_quote: The trees around the glade are bronze wood trees... fully grown, almost 40 feet above ground... He looks at a branch, growing at a natural 45-degree angle to the trunk with 8-inch leaves sprouting from it.

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia uses an illusion to trick the boar into approaching, and later stands with the captured boar next to Quinna Poul.
source_quote: Zephyr’s attempt at an illusion doesn’t trick the boar, but Zinnia’s does... A few hours later, Zinnia stands with the boar next to Quinna.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr kills the hag, finds the map of the local area, and decides the operation is lucrative after receiving the reward offer from Pasmarie Clee.
source_quote: Zephyr will have none of that and kills her... 'Reward is added to the other reward. And we get to find the chest. This is starting to be a very lucrative operation!'

subject: Plum Pie
fact: The plum pie in the hag’s gingerbread house is poisonous, as noted by Zinnia after sniffing it.
source_quote: He takes a sniff of the pie and realizes it is poisonous.

subject: Gingerbread
fact: Zinnia breaks off and eats a piece of the gingerbread from the door frame, concluding it is the genuine article.
source_quote: But then he decides that the frosting on the door frame must not be counterfeit, and the gingerbread must be the genuine article. So he breaks off a piece, chews, and smiles.

subject: Gnonsbim
fact: Gnonsbim, Captain of the Guard, asked Zephyr’s group to investigate bandits, and Glennddarc suspects he is running for re-election and has gone sweet on Pasmarie Clee.
source_quote: Well, we did talk to Gnonsbim, the Captain of the Guard, and he asked us to investigate them... 'Yes, Gnonsbim! He’s running for re-election and wants to show he’s a man of action... If you ask me, Gnonsbim has gone sweet on her.'

subject: Moot Hall Doors
fact: The Moot Hall doors are carved with the runes 'Ni te pharkalu, quo lun verra lu,' translated as 'If you see it, it’s not the right it,' reminding visitors that what you see may be an illusion.
source_quote: These doors open into the Feasting Hall... 'Ni te pharkalu, quo lun verra lu, ' with a helpful translation in common: 'If you see it, it’s not the right it.' He wonders for a minute, and it reminds Gnomes that what you see may be an illusion.

subject: Weasel
fact: A weasel jumps into Glennddarc’s lap, waking him with a grouchy yelp, then nuzzles his ear and flips on its back, baring its soft underbelly, prompting the gnome to stroke its fur with a bemused smile.
source_quote: A weasel jumps out from seemingly nowhere into the elder gnome's lap, waking him in a grouchy yelp. The weasel darts quickly to nuzzle the elder's ear, then flips on its back, baring its soft underbelly. Then, with a bemused smile, the gnome gently strokes the weasel's fur...

subject: Keenleene
fact: Keenleene, Founder of Sheernobb, is a living illusionary gnome statue who plays pipes, laughs heartily, winks, twirls, and hops, inviting all to join in merriment with pure joy.
source_quote: the stone figure of Keenleene transforms, coming to life with lifelike mischief... Keenleene begins to laugh heartily, a sound that resonates with pure joy. He picks up his pipes and starts playing a lively tune... He twirls and hops, inviting all who witness his performance to join in the merriment. The enchantment brings an undeniable sense of happiness and amusement, captivating.

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia, a spy, says, 'Bookstore owners either have a lot of information or none,' and learned that merchants of low-value goods, like books, tend to be the most well-connected.
source_quote: 'Bookstore owners either have a lot of information or none.' As a spy, he has learned that merchants of low-value goods, like books, tend to be the most well-connected.

subject: Djinibac’s Apothecary
fact: Djinibac’s Apothecary is one of the stores located around the circle formed by the road branches near the Moot Hall.
source_quote: The stores: 'Djinibac’s Apothecary, a Tabac Shop, Fiver Woodcarver, Peony’s Mill, and would you look at that a pond, Henker’s Shop, Naglo Crystal Divine Shop, and there is Grindin Books.'

subject: Tabac Shop
fact: A Tabac Shop is one of the stores located around the circle formed by the road branches near the Moot Hall.
source_quote: The stores: 'Djinibac’s Apothecary, a Tabac Shop, Fiver Woodcarver, Peony’s Mill, and would you look at that a pond, Henker’s Shop, Naglo Crystal Divine Shop, and there is Grindin Books.'

subject: Fiver Woodcarver
fact: Fiver Woodcarver is one of the stores located around the circle formed by the road branches near the Moot Hall.
source_quote: The stores: 'Djinibac’s Apothecary, a Tabac Shop, Fiver Woodcarver, Peony’s Mill, and would you look at that a pond, Henker’s Shop, Naglo Crystal Divine Shop, and there is Grindin Books.'

subject: Peony’s Mill
fact: Peony’s Mill is one of the stores located around the circle formed by the road branches near the Moot Hall.
source_quote: The stores: 'Djinibac’s Apothecary, a Tabac Shop, Fiver Woodcarver, Peony’s Mill, and would you look at that a pond, Henker’s Shop, Naglo Crystal Divine Shop, and there is Grindin Books.'

subject: Henker’s Shop
fact: Henker’s Shop is one of the stores located around the circle formed by the road branches near the Moot Hall, situated next to a pond.
source_quote: The stores: 'Djinibac’s Apothecary, a Tabac Shop, Fiver Woodcarver, Peony’s Mill, and would you look at that a pond, Henker’s Shop, Naglo Crystal Divine Shop, and there is Grindin Books.'

subject: Naglo Crystal Divine Shop
fact: Naglo Crystal Divine Shop is one of the stores located around the circle formed by the road branches near the Moot Hall.
source_quote: The stores: 'Djinibac’s Apothecary, a Tabac Shop, Fiver Woodcarver, Peony’s Mill, and would you look at that a pond, Henker’s Shop, Naglo Crystal Divine Shop, and there is Grindin Books.'

subject: Grindin Books
fact: Grindin Books is the final store listed, located at the end of the route, with a studded oak door and a welcoming sign.
source_quote: The stores: 'Djinibac’s Apothecary, a Tabac Shop, Fiver Woodcarver, Peony’s Mill, and would you look at that a pond, Henker’s Shop, Naglo Crystal Divine Shop, and there is Grindin Books.'
